readMethod: Opened both exact local PDFs with pypdf, verified their hashes/counts, and personally read the complete original-page text identified by the full-text logs. Rendered original pages with pdftoppm and personally inspected the readable full-page visuals listed separately, including meaningful tables, callouts and illustration labels. Extraction generation, cached research ledgers, other readers and image inventories are not counted as reading. All public citations in scope use physical PDF pages; no printed-page mapping is asserted.

readLogs.description: Personally read complete original-PDF text on these pages: collaboration and increasing independence, responsive relationship, modest material needs, how to read the book, source framing and individual children. Followed the listed communication and adult-response context; observation was not treated as a developmental test.

Personally read complete original-PDF text across Respect, boundaries, concentration, freedom of movement, attachment, crying and its checklist, Being their guide, Framing their view, the connection checklist and complete Going slow unit. Read continuation pages and retained context on necessary help, safety, feelings, warmth and the adult role; specific sensitive practices here are context, not additional advice for these entries.

Visually checked the appendix boundary to keep the guidelines separate from the previous table.

Personally read complete original-PDF text, including the full What do we do when we need to get through our daily tasks? and Montessori on a budget units: adult work, available assistance, ordinary connection, using existing resources and optional material choices.

Personally read the entire original PDF page, including the complete Physical disabilities or neurological differences unit, scope limit, individual timeline, as much help as needed, respectful treatment and named further resource. No universal family-contact advice is inferred.

Personally read complete original-PDF text: absorbent-mind framing, freedom with limits, adult responsibility, complete Independence and responsibility, Individual development, Respect and Observation. textPlacement.assessment: The recognizable activity-selection title and both topic rows make ages guides and retain support for developmental concerns in the summary itself. Observation is tied to interest, effort and fit, with a concrete option to set an unsuitable activity aside. The detailed paragraph attributes the books' help-seeking and specialist-scope framing without a diagnostic test or reassurance that waiting resolves a concern. The explicit Age, interest & context note makes this guidance about selection, without an expected skill for 6–9 months. Play & discovery and For you & your family both fit that purpose. The title names joining with help; the three topic rows preserve partial participation and an available adult, so independence is not presented as compulsory aloneness. The text invites noticing the part already being attempted, making room for effort and offering help. It distinguishes effort from discouraging frustration and retains Davies' exception for limited time or patience. The language offers assistance and does not require completion, deny warmth, or impose a specific tool or task. At 6–9 months, this is a general perspective in Everyday care, Play & discovery and For you & your family. It does not transfer a toddler skill or work-cycle expectation to a baby, or turn the child's participation into a deadline.
